summary.text: Oxidative phosphorylation is the metabolic pathway in which cells use enzymes to oxidize nutrients and release chemical energy to produce ATP.
Electrons pass along a chain of protein complexes, and the energy they release is used to move protons across a membrane, storing energy in a gradient.
ATP synthase taps that stored energy as protons flow back across the membrane, working as a rotary mechanical motor that turns ADP into ATP.

facts.label: ATP synthase
facts.value: Described as a rotary mechanical motor

facts.label: Main complexes
facts.value: Five main protein complexes in mitochondria

facts.label: Final electron acceptor
facts.value: Oxygen, at the end of the redox series

items.prompt: Almost all aerobic organisms carry out oxidative phosphorylation. Why is it so widespread?

options.label: It runs without any oxygen, so any cell can use it
It is the only pathway that makes NADH
It breaks glucose into pyruvate faster
It releases more energy than fermentation does

items.explain: The pathway is pervasive because it releases more energy than fermentation.

items.prompt: Electrons flow along the transport chain in a mitochondrion. What does that flow accomplish directly?

options.label: It joins phosphate onto ADP at each complex
It moves protons across the inner membrane, storing energy
It splits oxygen to supply more electrons
It rotates cytochrome c to build ATP

items.explain: The energy transferred by electrons through the chain is used to transport protons across the inner membrane.

items.prompt: Pressure built up on one side of a membrane is released through ATP synthase, spinning part of it. What flows through to turn it?

options.label: Protons moving back across the membrane
Oxygen molecules entering the matrix
ADP molecules moving back to the start
Electrons carried by iron atoms

items.explain: The reaction is driven by proton flow back across the membrane through ATP synthase, which forces rotation of part of the enzyme.

items.prompt: In a cell's power plant, energy-releasing reactions and ATP-making reactions are linked. What does the link mean?

options.label: ATP-making reactions can run alone without help
The two sets happen in separate compartments with no contact
Neither set of reactions can occur without the other
ATP making releases the energy that drives electron flow

items.explain: The two sets of reactions are coupled, meaning one cannot occur without the other.

items.prompt: Besides ATP, running this pathway also produces something that can damage cells. What is it?

options.label: Excess ADP that clogs the membrane
Reactive oxygen species, such as superoxide
Lactic acid from the fermentation side
Extra glucose that overloads the cell

items.explain: It produces reactive oxygen species such as superoxide and hydrogen peroxide, propagating free radicals that damage cells.

items.prompt: In real cells the ATP produced falls short of the theoretical maximum. Why?

options.label: Oxygen is used up before the chain ends
ATP synthase runs backward half the time
Cytochrome c loses its iron atom
Some protons leak across the membrane

items.explain: These yields are theoretical maximums; in practice some protons leak across the membrane, lowering the yield of ATP.
